  Evidence of absence: The PR's manifest hunk inserts changelog.d/6323-check-triage-isolated-diagnosis.md (a file that already existed on the base branch — verified via glob, changelog.d/6323-check-triage-isolated-diagnosis.md is present and was not part of this PR's file set per pr_changed_files.txt). The new changelog file from this PR, changelog.d/6364-triage-routing-metadata-neutralize.md (verified present in the filesystem via glob, and listed in pr_changed_files.txt), is absent from the manifest. After this PR merges, the manifest will list 6323 but not 6364, leaving the source tree and the manifest out of sync until the next workspace_init.sh run regenerates the manifest. The review-conflict manifest-union path in scripts/review_conflict_prepare.sh:203-234 (MANIFEST_UNION_PATH=.ai/.workspace_source_manifest.txt) will compute stale two-sided unions on every PR that conflicts on the manifest until that next materialize, which is exactly the per-run-overhead shape the manifest is meant to avoid.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Hardening suggestion, scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:451: When the neutralized diagnosis contains `<!--`, GitHub's markdown renderer decodes the entity back to `<` outside code fences, which restores a valid `<!-- ... -->` HTML comment in the rendered body. The raw-body parsers used by the orchestrator (resolve_integration_ref.sh, security_dependency.py, orchestrate_lib.py TARGET_BRANCH_LINE_RE) read the raw body, so they are safe; the test only asserts against the raw body. A future tool that consumes the GitHub API's rendered body_html field, or a human reader, would still see the spoofed comment. The fallback path places the evidence inside a code fence, but the model-quotation path concatenates raw model output into the body without a code fence, so the renderer would interpret `<!--` as a comment opener. Suggested minimal fix: After the existing `re.subn(r"<!--", "<!--", diagnosis)`, also encode the `-->` closer, e.g. add `diagnosis, _ = re.subn(r"-->", "-->", diagnosis)`. The raw body then never contains the substring `-->` outside the trusted marker section, so a render-side decode cannot form a comment. HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
